related_questions.question: Is COVID considered a disability under ADA?

text_blocks.snippet: While a temporary case of COVID-19 is not typically considered a disability under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), "Long COVID," which involves lingering symptoms and limitations, may qualify as a disability. The ADA requires an individualized assessment to determine if a person's condition substantially limits a major life activity.

list.title: Temporary COVID-19:
list.snippet: A short-term illness with typical recovery is generally not covered under the ADA.

list.title: Long COVID:
list.snippet: This refers to ongoing health problems following a COVID-19 infection. If these problems significantly limit major life activities, like breathing, concentrating, or working, it could be considered a disability under the ADA.

list.title: Individualized Assessment:
list.snippet: Each case of Long COVID is evaluated individually. The severity and duration of symptoms, as well as their impact on the individual's ability to perform daily tasks, are considered.
